source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on quant-ph/0404042 (pp.1-6,8-9), hep-th/0203101 (pp.1,6,8-11,35), hep-th/0402058 (pp.1-11), 0804.2182 (pp.1-12), 2309.07436 (pp.1-8,14-16,21-24,28-30,32), 1804.10623 (pp.1-12), 2602.03606 (pp.1-17). published_statement: Bekenstein quant-ph/0404042 p.1: 'In 1981 I proposed [1] that the entropy of a complete physical system in asymptotically flat D = 4 spacetime, whose total mass-energy is E, and which fits inside a sphere of radius R, is necessarily bounded from above: S <= 2 pi E R / hbar c. (1)' ... 'E is to be interpreted as the gravitating energy of the system'; 'the universal bound is relevant only for weakly self-gravitating isolated physical systems'; p.2: 'There is no controversy today as to the validity of bound (1) for complete, weakly self-gravitating, isolated objects in ordinary asymptotically flat spacetime.' SATURATION, Bousso hep-th/0203101 p.9: 'The application of the bound to strongly gravitating systems is complicated by the difficulty of defining the radius of the system in a highly curved geometry. At least for spherically symmetric systems, however, this is not a problem, as one may define R in terms of the surface area. A Schwarzschild black hole in four dimensions has R = 2E. Hence, its Bekenstein entropy, S = A/4 = pi R^2, exactly saturates the Bekenstein bound (Bekenstein, 1981). In D > 4, black holes come to within a factor 2/(D-2) of saturating the bound (Bousso, 2001).' NO G: Bousso hep-th/0402058 p.5: 'The absence of Newton's constant in Bekenstein's bound is notable ... the bound remains nontrivial when gravity is turned off completely (G = 0).' PROVEN FORM, Casini 0804.2182 p.6: S(rho_V) - S(rho0_V) <= tr(K rho_V) - tr(K rho0_V), equivalent to positivity of relative entropy; 'for an object far enough from the boundaries in a half space the relation (17) approaches (1) with lambda = 2 pi'.
published_hypotheses: COMPLETE system: E is the TOTAL gravitating mass-energy, including rest energy, walls/confining structure and ground-state energy (quant-ph/0404042 p.1, Sec. II p.2, Sec. VI.B p.8: 'in the universal bound, E must include the ground state energy')
WEAKLY SELF-GRAVITATING, isolated (quant-ph/0404042 p.1; hep-th/0203101 p.6 'they apply only when gravity is weak', p.8 'For any weakly gravitating matter system in asymptotically flat space')
asymptotically flat, D = 4 (quant-ph/0404042 p.1; D > 4 handled separately, p.2)

R = radius of the smallest sphere circumscribing the system, with a time slicing in which space is almost Euclidean (hep-th/0203101 p.8); no consensus on R (circumscribing vs shortest dimension) or on the coefficient (2 pi vs larger) (Casini 0804.2182 p.3; quant-ph/0404042 p.1 'a larger numerical coefficient must be accepted' under quantum buoyancy)
not valid inside black holes or for large pieces of the universe (quant-ph/0404042 p.1-2)

SATURATION clause: holds for Schwarzschild in D = 4 with R defined by the horizon area, i.e. by extrapolating the bound to a strongly gravitating, spherically symmetric object (hep-th/0203101 p.9, p.10 'if the latter is assumed to hold for strongly gravitating systems')

PROVEN FORM (Casini 2008; Longo-Xu 2018; Longo 2025; Hollands-Longo-Morsella 2026): S is a vacuum-subtracted entropy / vacuum relative entropy, E a vacuum-subtracted (modular) energy, R the distance to a Rindler boundary or the half-width of the localisation region; flat space, fixed geometry (0804.2182 p.8: 'in both of these proofs the static limit is crucial, what means a flat space limit')
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED -- bounds.py:315 and bounds.py:49/97 'saturated by black holes' (hypothesis listed in canonical as 'black-hole saturation (K = 0)'): the published clause is SCHWARZSCHILD IN D = 4 (hep-th/0203101 p.9). Computed here (rederive C, D, B): Reissner-Nordstrom, spherically symmetric so R is unambiguous, gives S/bound = r+/(2M) < 1 for every Q != 0 (1/2 at extremality); Kerr gives 1 for R = r+ but 1/sqrt(2) (areal R) or 1/2 (equatorial circumscribing R) at extremality, so its saturation is convention-dependent; D > 4 Schwarzschild gives 2/(D-2). 'Black holes' is a larger class than the one on which saturation holds.

DROPPED -- bounds.py:315 / bounds.py:97: the saturating object lies outside the bound's own validity class (weakly self-gravitating; quant-ph/0404042 p.1, hep-th/0203101 pp.6, 9-10). The saturation is an extrapolation, stated as such by Bousso; the tree records it without that hypothesis.

DROPPED (bounds.py only) -- canonical hypothesis 'entropy in region of radius R with energy E' (bounds.py:310 comment, row bounds.py:315) omits 'complete system / E total gravitating energy' and 'R circumscribing radius'. Page 1804.10623 p.2 shows that with E the field energy inside a bounded region the bound has counterexamples (Casimir E < 0, near-ground mixtures, N species, conducting plates, coaxial loop). massform.py keeps the hypothesis: E = Mc^2 (rest energy included, massform.py:460-461, 2020-2023) with R = 1 m named as H-R (massform.py:830, 2010).

NONE MATERIAL -- massform.py:460-470 quotes the bound as READ (quant-ph/0404042 Eq.1, confirmed verbatim here) and holds it with Hayden-Wang's caution; the Hayden-Wang wording at massform.py:1398-1412 matches 2309.07436v3 pp.1,3-4 as read here. 'widely accepted proven version is Casini's' is Hayden-Wang's sentence, not an added claim.

DISCREPANCY IN THE TREE'S CODING, NOT IN THE SOURCE (bounds.py:24-27, 315): Bekenstein is coded S = 0 ('state-dependent RHS: no') and B = 1 ('a negative constant'). The published RHS 2 pi E R/(hbar c) contains E, the system's total energy (in the proven form an expectation value in the state, <K> or 2 pi R <H>: 0804.2182 p.6, 2602.03606 Prop. 2.1), and it is non-negative for a complete system. Casini is coded S = 1 although for the Rindler wedge its RHS is 2 pi integral x T00, the Bekenstein form (2309.07436 eq. 1.3). Recorded for the owner; not graded here, and not quoted as an error of the external result.

ADJACENT SITE (not a canonical owner) -- nopath.py:229 'Independent route to the same number' and nopath.py:234-235 'THE BITS ARE THE MASS': the two routes agree only at saturation, i.e. for Schwarzschild at R = r_s (verified, rederive A and E); for weakly gravitating matter the Bekenstein figure is an upper bound that real systems reach at best within about an order of magnitude (hep-th/0203101 p.9).

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (18 checks). (A) Schwarzschild D=4: 2 pi r_s Mc^2/(hbar c) == A c^3/(4 G hbar) == 4 pi G M^2/(hbar c) symbolically -- saturation is exact. (B) D-dim Schwarzschild ratio = 2/(D-2) symbolically (1, 2/3, 1/2, 1/4 at D = 4, 5, 6, 10), matching Bousso p.9. (C) Reissner-Nordstrom ratio = r+/(2M): 1, 0.9330, 0.7179, 0.5000 at Q/M = 0, .5, .9, 1 -- NOT saturated for Q != 0. (D) Kerr: R = r+ gives 1 for all a (identity r+^2 + a^2 = 2 M r+); areal R gives 0.7071 and equatorial circumscribing R gives 0.5 at extremality -- saturation convention-dependent. (E) The tree's numbers reproduce from its own constants: 1.803836e45 bits (70 kg, 1 m), 1.578356e45 (0.875 m), ratio 7478.4651, break-even 1.337173e-4 m; nopath.bekenstein_bits and nopath.routes_agree() agree. (F) Weak gravity 2GM/(c^2R) = 1.04e-25; Bekenstein figure is 1.04e-25 of the holographic A/4 at 1 m. (G) T_CMB move changes the ratio by -7.3e-6.

later_literature.what: Proves a precise form: vacuum-subtracted entropy <= vacuum-subtracted modular energy, i.e. positivity of relative entropy; reduces to lambda = 2 pi for an object far from a half-space boundary; resolves the species problem; holds only in fixed (flat) geometry. The proven statement is about redefined S, E, R, not the 1981 quantities.

Counterexamples for many definitions of system/R/E/S, including total von Neumann entropy of vacuum-outside-R states (violation for x = 2 pi R E < 1.15e-4); Casini's redefinition 'finally enabled a proof for this particular formulation'; Longo-Xu made it rigorous.

Classical and quantum Unruh-channel capacities obey the decoder's Bekenstein bound; zero-bit capacity does not (unbounded in species number d) unless the encoder is also restricted (Blanco-Casini form). The 'limit on stored information' reading is folklore. The tree already holds this caution.

later_literature.ref: S. Hollands, R. Longo, G. Morsella, arXiv 2602.03606 (2026); R. Longo, arXiv 2409.14408 (CMP 406, 95 (2025)) restated there
later_literature.what: Rigorous S(Phi|B) <= 2 pi R E(Phi|B) for Klein-Gordon wave packets (and Majorana one-particle states) localised in B, R the half-width, and Longo's general Bekenstein-type bound -log Delta_H(B) <= 2 pi R P for local Poincare-covariant nets; fails without localisation (boundary term Gamma_Phi).
Bekenstein bound derived (up to O(1), rigorously in hep-th/0210295) from the generalized covariant bound in weak gravity; contains no G -- supports bounds.py's DOCKET 4 re-coding G 1 -> 0.

lacked_data: What Bekenstein lacked in 1981 was not a measured datum -- the bound has no empirical input beyond hbar and c -- but (i) a definition of S, E and R that makes sense in QFT (supplied by Marolf-Minic-Ross 2004, Casini 2008, Longo-Xu 2018, Longo 2025); (ii) the quantum-buoyancy objection (Unruh-Wald 1982), which Bekenstein answers only with 'a larger numerical coefficient' (quant-ph/0404042 p.1); (iii) the species-problem resolution (Casini 0804.2182 p.6-7). EVIDENCE THAT HAVING IT CHANGES THE CONCLUSION: yes for the bare 1981 form under naive definitions -- Page 1804.10623 exhibits violations -- and the proven version bounds a vacuum-subtracted entropy by a modular energy, not the 1981 S by the 1981 E R. EVIDENCE THAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE TREE'S CONCLUSIONS: (a) K = 0 rests on the Schwarzschild identity, an algebraic fact independent of the QFT formalisation (rederive A); (b) G = 0 is confirmed at source by Bousso and by Hayden-Wang ('lambda ... independent of G_N', p.1); (c) massform's instance is a complete, weakly gravitating system (2GM/c^2R = 1e-25) far outside every published counterexample regime (x ~ 1e45), and massform already declines to read the figure as an information capacity (Hayden-Wang); (d) 'it bounds by energy; it supplies none' is a logical property of an upper bound and survives every formulation read. What later work DOES remove is the tree's generalisation 'saturated by black holes': only Schwarzschild D = 4 saturates convention-independently, and it does so outside the bound's own weak-gravity class.
grade_evidence: The bound as massform.py uses it (S <= 2 pi E R/(hbar c) with E = Mc^2, R = 1 m, read as an upper bound and not as a capacity) matches the published statement and hypotheses, and every figure re-derives (1.8038e45 bits, 1.58e45, 7478, 0.134 mm; no moved datum moves any of them). The NARROWING is bounds.py's saturation clause: 'saturated by black holes' (bounds.py:315, :49, :97) holds at source only for Schwarzschild in D = 4 (hep-th/0203101 p.9), and is computed here to FAIL for Reissner-Nordstrom (ratio r+/2M < 1 for Q != 0, 1/2 extremal, with R unambiguous by spherical symmetry), to be convention-dependent for Kerr, and to be 2/(D-2) in D > 4; and the saturating object lies outside the weakly-self-gravitating hypothesis that the tree does not carry (quant-ph/0404042 p.1; hep-th/0203101 pp.6,9-10). No tree pin moves: K = 0 needs one saturating case and Schwarzschild is one; G = 0 is confirmed at source. A coding discrepancy (S = 0, B = 1 against a published RHS containing the state's energy) is recorded for the owner and is not part of this grade.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: bounds.py's note restricted to 'saturated by Schwarzschild (D = 4), by extrapolation to strong gravity with R the areal radius' with the weak-gravity hypothesis named -- the external result itself would then be used exactly as published. To OPEN or WRONG for the K = 0 pin: a reading of Bekenstein 1981 (PRD 23, 287) at source showing that its saturation clause or its R prescription differs from Bousso's restatement (not available here; the classic is NAMED-NOT-READ); or a ruling that the K slot means 'saturated within the bound's own validity class', in which case no weakly gravitating system is known to saturate it exactly (Bousso p.9: 'within an order of magnitude') and K = 0 would need re-examination. To DATA-DEPENDENT: none foreseeable -- the bound has no moved or contested empirical input.
